# v0.2.3 — Charging reliability and lower Recorder load

This maintenance release fixes charging-current, serial recovery and PV
automation behavior. The minimum remains **Home Assistant 2026.9.0**;
existing **0.2.x** entries, devices and entity IDs can be kept.

## Updating PV automations

After the integration installs the updated blueprint, reload existing
**Charge from PV surplus** automations. The automation now replaces an
in-flight current adjustment when a newer power budget arrives. Existing
0.2.2 input selections remain valid.

When upgrading from **0.2.1 or earlier**, also select the wallbox's **Charging
paused** input, save the automation and reload it. Until selected, that
automation sends no current commands. Edited blueprint copies are preserved;
apply the changes manually. See the
[blueprint update instructions](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron/blob/v0.2.3/docs/blueprints.md#updating-existing-blueprint-automations).

## Charging and serial fixes

- Home Assistant control permissions are checked for every charging-current
  target, including unlimited mode, before any writes occur.
- Lost replies no longer trigger automatic transport write retries that
  bypass register cooldowns. Reads retain their bounded retry budget.
- Cancelled bus searches stop and release the port. Reconfiguration handles
  exclusive serial ownership and restores the previous connection on failure.
- Rejected setpoints preserve the accepted resume current. A phase-change
  pause remembers the actual current, and phase-switch cooldowns are checked
  before charging is paused.
- Optional blueprint file failures no longer prevent integration setup.
  Blueprint updates preserve user edits and replace files atomically.

## Recorder and maintenance

Unchanged polls no longer trigger unnecessary entity updates; availability
and write-repair changes remain visible. A complete lean Recorder profile
keeps total-energy and total-power history while excluding unwanted detail.
It produced **88% fewer state rows** in the documented synthetic charging-day
comparison. The default 30-second measurement interval remains unchanged.

The [Recorder guide](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron/blob/v0.2.3/docs/recorder.md)
explains retention, detail exclusions and free-space monitoring. These require
user configuration: the integration does not change global Recorder settings,
delete existing history or impose a database size cap. History purges do not
remove long-term statistics. Accelerated SQLite tests cover repeated
purge/repack cycles, preserved hourly statistics and database integrity.

Weekly compatibility checks test the supported HA matrix and the next HA
version without opening routine dependency PRs. Security updates remain
enabled. The checks use the pymodbus version selected by Home Assistant.
Repository changes now require a current-commit security review before merge.

## Compatibility and package

Validation covers **HA 2026.9.0**, **2026.10.0** and **2026.11.0b1**, with
541/541/543 passing tests and 99.44% statement/branch coverage. November
compatibility is beta-tested; this is not a claim of testing November stable
or HA 2026.12. Physical-wallbox validation remains outstanding, and accelerated
Recorder tests are not a wall-clock or disk-full soak test.

The domain remains **`mennekes_amtron_rtu`**. Upgrading from **0.1.0** requires
the separate [domain migration](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron/blob/v0.2.3/docs/upgrading.md).

One installation archive serves HACS and the Marketplace:
**`ha-mennekes-amtron.zip`**. Checksums, build metadata and an SPDX SBOM
accompany the package.
